title.narrative: Health Sector Enhancement Program

description.narrative: The proposed program will support Georgia's health sector reforms, which will prioritize primary health care (PHC) and specialized outpatient and diagnostic services through sector regulation, redefining health care benefits, improving strategic purchasing mechanisms, and restructuring governance and organizational arrangements, to enhance the sector's operational efficiency, service delivery, and financial sustainability. The program is aligned with Strategy 2030 of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and supports the operational priorities on addressing remaining poverty and reducing inequalities; accelerating progress in gender equality; tackling climate change, building climate and disaster resilience, and enhancing environmental sustainability; and strengthening governance and institutional capacity. The program is consistent with ADB's country partnership strategy for Georgia to support the government's development priority for human capital development as well as climate change action. The proposed stand-alone policy-based loan (PBL) comprises two tranches amounting to a total of $50 million from ADB's ordinary capital resources.

title.narrative: Output 1

description.narrative: 1.1. To improve access and clarity of state-funded benefits offered to the population for PHC, specialized outpatient and diagnostic benefits, the government: (i) enhanced the benefits package of PHC services, ensuring that included services are patient-centered, gender-sensitive, and responsive to the population's health needs, especially to the needs of the poor, women, and vulnerable groups; (i) defined beneficiary groups that are eligible for free PHC and state-subsidized specialized care and diagnostic services, giving more benefits and greater financial protection to the poor, women, and vulnerable groups; and (ii) through MOH defined and approved the phased introduction of the enhanced PHC benefit package following the PHC roadmap developed with WHO support.

title.narrative: Output 2

description.narrative: 2.1. To improve and ensure a continuum of health service provision for the patient across levels of care, the government through MOH established the gatekeeping function for PHC with clinical care pathways for four most-prevalent noncommunicable disease conditions to regulate referrals from primary care to specialized outpatient, diagnostic, and hospital services, and to significantly reduce patient self-referrals.

Policy 4: Governance and accountability for the quality of delivered services improved Outcome 1: By April 2026, at least 5 PHC-related quality indicators are defined and routinely reported on the MOH/NHA website (2023 baseline: 0).
Action 2: To improve the availability of healthcare providers and geographic access to PHC services for the population, the government through MOH will approve and implement the PHC workforce plan. Target date: 2025-04-30
Action 3: To improve the quality of care by health professionals, the government through MOH will mandate certification of CME and CPD requirements for medical personnel, and implement clinical decision support certification courses. Target date: 2025-04-30

Target date: 2025-04-30
